source_text: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπέμεινεν ὁ κύριος παραδοῦναι τὴν σάρκα εἰς καταφθοράν, ἵνα τῇ ἀφέσει τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἁγνισθῶμεν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ῥαντίσματος αὐτοῦ. γέγραπται γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἅ μὲν πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ, ἃ δὲ πρὸς ἡμᾶς, λέγει δὲ οὕτως: Ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν: τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν: ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἄφωνος ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτόν. οὐκοῦν ὑπερευχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι καὶ τὰ παρεληλυθότα ἡμῖν ἐγνώρισεν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐνεστῶσιν ἡμᾶς ἐσόφισεν. καὶ εἰς τὰ μέλλοντα οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀσύνετοι. λέγει δὲ ἡ γραφή: Οὐκ ἀδίκως ἐκτείνεται δίκτυα πτερωτοῖς. τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι δικαίως ἀπολεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἔχων ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης γνῶσιν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὁδὸν σκότους ἀποσυνέχει. ἔτι δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ἀδελφοί μου: εἰ ὁ κύριος ὑπέμεινεν παθεῖν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν, ὢν παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου κύριος ᾧ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ̓ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν: πῶς οὖν ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὸ χειρὸς ἀνθρώπων παθεῖν; μάθετε. οἱ προφῆται, ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντες τὴν χάριν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπροφήτευσαν: αὐτὸς δέ, ἵνα καταργήσῃ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν δείξῃ, ὅτι ὲν σαρκὶ ἕδει αὐτὸν φανερωθῆναι, ὑπέμεινεν, ἵνα τοῖς πατράσιν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἀποδῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ τὸν λαὸν τὸν καινὸν ἑτοιμάζων ἐπιδείξῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤν, ὅτι τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτὸς ποιήσας κρινεῖ. πέρας γέ τοι διδάσκων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τηλικαῦτα τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ποιῶν ἐκήρυσσεν, καὶ ὑπερηγάπησεν αὐτόν. ὅτε δὲ τοὺς ἰδίους ἀποστόλους τοὺς μέλλοντας κηρύσσειν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον αὐτοῦ ἐξελέξατο, ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνομωτέρους, ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθεν καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς, τότε ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἦλθεν ἐν σαρκί, οὐδ’ ἄν πως οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐσώθησαν βλέποντες αὐτόν, ὅτε τὸν μέλλοντα μὴ εἶναι ἥλιον, ἔργου τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχοντα, ἐμβλέποντες οὐκ ἰσχύουσιν εἰς τὰς ἀκτῖνας αὐτοῦ ἀντοφθαλμῆσαι: οὐκοῦν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο ἐν σαρκὶ ἦλθεν, ἵνα τὸ τέλειον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀνακεφαλαιώσῃ τοῖς διώξασιν ἐν θανάτῳ τοὺς προφήτας αὐτοῦ. οὐκοῦν εἰς τοῦτο ὑπέμεινεν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τὴν πληγὴν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐξ αὐτῶν: Ὅταν πατάξωσιν τὸν ποιμένα ἑαυτῶν, τότε ἀπολεῖται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης. αὐτὸς δὲ ἠθέλησεν οὕτω παθεῖν: ἔδει γάρ, ἵνα ἐπὶ ξύλου πάθῃ. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφητεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ. Φεῖσαί μου τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπὸ ῥομφαίας, καί: Καθήλωσόν μου τὰς σάρκας, ὅτι πονηρευομένων συναγωγαὶ ἐπανέστησάν νέστησάν μοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, τέθεικά μου τὸν νῶτον εἰς μάστιγας, τὰς δὲ σιαγόνας εἰς ῥαπίσματα. τὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν μου ἔθηκα ὡς στερεὰν πέτραν.
pass_a_gloss: For the Lord endured to deliver his flesh to destruction, so that by the forgiveness of sins we might be purified, which is in the blood of his sprinkling. For it is written about him, the things concerning Israel and the things concerning us, and he says thus: He was wounded because of our iniquities and bruised because of our sins; by his bruise we were healed. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb, silent before the one shearing him. Therefore, we ought to give great thanks to the Lord, because he made known to us the things that have passed and in the present things he has made us wise, and we are not without understanding concerning the things to come. And the scripture says: The net is not spread in vain for winged creatures. This it says, that justly a man will perish who, having knowledge of the way of righteousness, draws himself away to the way of darkness. And yet, my brothers, if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, being Lord of all the world, to whom God said from the foundation of the world: Let us make man according to our image and likeness; how then did he endure to suffer by the hand of men? Learn. The prophets, having grace from him, prophesied concerning him. And he, so that he might abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, endured, because it was necessary for him to be revealed in flesh, so that he might give the promise to the fathers and prepare for himself a new people, showing himself on earth, because having made the resurrection, he will judge. For he taught Israel and did such great signs and wonders and preached, and he loved them exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles, who were going to preach his gospel, being more lawless than all sin, so that he might show that he did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, then he revealed himself to be the Son of God. For if he had not come in flesh, men would not have been saved by seeing him, when they cannot even look at the sun, which is a work of his hands, because they cannot gaze at its rays. Therefore, the Son of God came in flesh, so that he might sum up the perfect things concerning sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore, he endured. For God says concerning the wound of his flesh, that it is from them: When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will perish. But he himself willed to suffer thus, for it was necessary for him to suffer on wood. For the one prophesying about him says: Spare my soul from the sword, and: Pierce my flesh, because the assemblies of the wicked rose up against me. And again he says: Behold, I have set my back for scourges, my cheeks for slaps. And I have set my face like a hard rock.

pass_b_english: The Lord endured giving his flesh over to destruction so that we might be purified by the forgiveness of sins, which lies in the blood of his sprinkling. For it is written about him — the things concerning Israel and the things concerning us — and he says this: "He was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5). "Like a lamb led to the slaughter, and like a sheep silent before its shearers" (Isaiah 53:7). Therefore we ought to give great thanks to the Lord, because he has made known to us the things that have passed and in the present he has made us wise, and we are not without understanding concerning the things to come. And Scripture says: "A net is not spread unjustly for winged creatures" (Proverbs 1:17). This means that a person will justly perish who, having knowledge of the way of righteousness, draws himself away to the way of darkness. And yet, my brothers, if the Lord endured suffering for our soul — he who is Lord of all the world, to whom God said from the foundation of the world, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" — how then did he endure suffering at the hands of men? Learn this: the prophets, having grace from him, prophesied about him. And he, in order to abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, endured, because it was necessary for him to be revealed in flesh, so that he might give back the promise to the fathers and prepare for himself a new people, showing himself on earth, because having brought about the resurrection he will judge. For he taught Israel and did such great signs and wonders and preached, and he loved them exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles who were going to preach his gospel — men more lawless than any sin — so that he might show that he did not come to call the righteous but sinners, then he revealed himself to be the Son of God. For if he had not come in flesh, men would not have been saved by seeing him; when they cannot even look at the sun, which is a work of his hands, because they cannot gaze at its rays. Therefore the Son of God came in flesh so that he might sum up the perfecting of sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore he endured. For God says concerning the wound of his flesh that it is from them: "When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will perish" (Zechariah 13:7). But he himself willed to suffer thus, for it was necessary for him to suffer on wood. For the one prophesying about him says: "Spare my soul from the sword" (Psalms 22:20), and: "Pierce my flesh, because the assemblies of the wicked rose up against me" (Psalms 22:16). And again he says: "Behold, I have set my back for scourges, my cheeks for slaps. And I have set my face like a hard rock" (Isaiah 50:6).
